title: The comparison unit is an isomorphism
statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme. For every sheaf of sets $F$ on $X_{\Et}$ the unit
$\eta_F\colon F	o
u_{X,*}
u_X^*F$ is an isomorphism. Consequently
$
u_X^*\colon\Sh(X_{\Et})	o\Sh(X_{\Proet})$ is fully faithful: for sheaves
$F,F'$ on $X_{\Et}$ the map
$\Hom(F,F')	o\Hom(
u_X^*F,
u_X^*F')$, $\varphi\mapsto
u_X^*\varphi$, is
bijective.

proof.text: Fix an etale sheaf F and an arbitrary etale object U. The direct image of [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism] is restriction. Apply [lem-cbc-comparison-pullback-sections] and write its comparison isomorphism as p and its section equivalence as e. Its final clause says e composed with the U-component of p and the actual comparison unit equals the usual etale section map. Its preceding clause states that this usual map is bijective (the restriction identification has already been proved inside that theorem). Since e and the component of p are bijective, cancellation shows that the actual unit at U is bijective. No coefficient-ring or nonemptiness assumption is used.

proof.text: The component bijections of step 1 give an invertible natural transformation of presheaves by Mathlib NatIso.isIso_of_isIso_app and isIso_iff_bijective. The sheaf-to-presheaf functor is fully faithful and reflects isomorphisms, hence each sheaf unit is invertible. Equivalently, naturality of the component inverses follows by composing the unit naturality square with the inverses. This also covers the empty scheme.

source.place: Tag 099T, lemma-fully-faithful, using Tag 0GLZ, lemma-describe-pullback-from-etale; explicit adjunction argument for full faithfulness

proof.text: The unit is a natural isomorphism by step 2. Apply Mathlib Adjunction.fullyFaithfulLOfIsIsoUnit to the adjunction of [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism], then Functor.FullyFaithful.map_bijective. This is the adjunction Hom argument: a morphism from inverse image F to inverse image F-prime corresponds to a morphism from F to direct image of inverse image F-prime; invertibility of the latter unit gives the required unique morphism from F to F-prime.
